retirement.closing: {{venue}} shuts down on {{date}}. Sync one last time and withdraw your funds before then — once the API is gone, any trade left there can no longer be imported. Nothing already imported is deleted: your {{venue}} history stays and keeps counting.
retirement.closed: {{venue}} closed on {{date}}, so syncing is off. Your {{venue}} history is kept in full and still counts in every analytic for the period it covers.

coverage.BITUNIX: Full history since you opened the account.
coverage.BINGX: Only ~the last 30 days — BingX's API serves no older fills, so sync regularly; older trades can't be recovered.
coverage.BITMART: Recent history only — BitMart's API serves a limited window of fills, so sync regularly; older trades can't be recovered. Only the API key is needed (read-only). BitMart shuts down on 2026-08-26.
coverage.BINANCE_FUTURES: About the last 3 months. Binance keeps fills for 6 months, but the endpoint that reveals which symbols you traded only goes back 3 — so sync at least quarterly. Funding is imported, so PnL is complete.
coverage.BYBIT: Up to 2 years of fills, pulled in 7-day windows. Funding is imported alongside the trades, so PnL is complete.
coverage.OKX: The last 90 days of closed positions — OKX serves no older ones, so sync regularly. PnL, fees and funding all come from OKX directly. Needs the API passphrase as well as key and secret.
coverage.BITGET: The last 90 days of closed positions (Unified Trading Account). PnL, fees and funding come from Bitget directly. Needs the API passphrase as well as key and secret.
coverage.BITGET_CLASSIC: The last 90 days of closed positions, for a Bitget account NOT upgraded to a Unified Trading Account. A UTA key will be rejected here — use plain Bitget for those. Needs the API passphrase as well as key and secret.
coverage.KRAKEN_FUTURES: Kraken's separate futures platform — kept apart from any Kraken spot history, since it is a different account with its own balance. Linear perpetuals (PF_) only. Fees are NOT imported: Kraken states the fee values its API returns no longer reflect what was charged, so net PnL here reads slightly better than reality.
coverage.KRAKEN_SPOT: Kraken's spot platform — a different account and balance from Kraken Futures, kept as its own venue. Positions are rebuilt from your trade history, so a holding you have never fully sold does not appear until you close it. Real fees are imported; there is no funding on spot, and PnL is recorded in the pair's quote currency (often USD or EUR, never converted).
coverage.GATEIO_FUTURES: Closed positions with PnL already split into trading result, funding and fees — the cleanest source here. Depth depends on what Gate.io retains.
coverage.MEXC_FUTURES: Closed positions with PnL and leverage. Note: MEXC restricts futures API access, so a new key may be rejected — if syncing fails with a permissions error, that limit is why, not your setup.
coverage.KUCOIN_FUTURES: The last 3 months of closed positions, pulled in 7-day windows. PnL, fees and funding come from KuCoin directly. Needs the API passphrase as well as key and secret.
coverage.QUANTFURY: Your entire history — whatever is in the uploaded PDF (no API, so nothing syncs automatically).
coverage.JOURNAL_CSV: Whatever you import — a manual CSV of closed positions, e.g. from exchanges that no longer exist. Nothing syncs automatically.

setupHelp.show: How do I get these credentials?
setupHelp.title: Creating a read-only {{venue}} API key
setupHelp.readOnly: READ-ONLY KEY: enable only read/query permissions. Never enable trading. Never enable withdrawal.

steps: Sign in at bitunix.com, hover the profile icon (top right) and click **API** to open API Management.
Click **Create API**.
In **Note**, type a name you will recognise later — the label you gave this source is a good choice.
Under **Purpose**, choose **Bind third-party app**.
Confirm with the email verification code Bitunix sends.
Copy the **API Key** and **Secret Key** into the fields above.
BITUNIX.permissions: Set **Permission** to **Read-only**, and nothing else — no trading, no withdrawal.
BITUNIX.ip: Optional; Bitunix accepts up to 20 addresses per key. Leave it empty if you self-host on a connection whose IP changes, or bind your server's address if it is fixed.
BITUNIX.secret: The **Secret Key** is shown only once, right after creation. Copy it before closing the dialog.

steps: Turn on 2FA first — BingX refuses to create API keys without it.
Open **API Management** from the profile icon, select **Main account**, then click **Create API**.
Name the key and pass the 2FA check.
Copy the **API Key** and **Secret Key** into the fields above.
BINGX.permissions: Tick **Read** and nothing else. Leave **Spot Trading** and **Perpetual Futures Trading** off, and never grant withdrawal.
BINGX.ip: Optional. A key that only has **Read** never expires on BingX even with no IP bound, so leaving it blank is fine for a self-hosted setup.
BINGX.secret: The **Secret Key** appears once, on the confirmation screen. Copy it immediately.
BINGX.note: BingX's API only serves about the last 30 days of fills, so sync regularly — older trades cannot be recovered later.

steps: Sign in, open the profile menu and go to **API Management**.
Create a new key and type any phrase as the **Memo** — BitMart requires one for its signature. tradelog does not use it, but save it anyway.
Complete the email and 2FA verification.
Copy the **Access Key** and **Secret Key** into the fields above.
BITMART.permissions: **Read-only** is on by default and is the only authority to leave enabled. Never **Trade**, never **Withdraw**.
BITMART.ip: Optional, and recommended by BitMart. Leave it blank if your address changes.
BITMART.secret: Copy both keys before pressing **Confirm** — the **Secret Key** cannot be viewed again afterwards.
BITMART.note: Reading BitMart only ever sends the API key (its private reads are keyed, not signed), but the form still stores a secret. BitMart closes on 2026-08-26, so import what you have before then.

steps: Open your Futures account first if you have not already: a key created before Futures existed cannot read Futures data.
Profile icon → **Account** → **API Management** → **Create API**.
Choose **System-generated**, so Binance hands you an API key and a secret.
Label the key, then confirm with your 2FA device or passkey.
Copy the **API Key** and **Secret Key** into the fields above.
BINANCE_FUTURES.permissions: Leave only **Enable Reading** ticked — it is on by default and covers everything tradelog reads, futures history included. Do not tick **Enable Futures**, **Enable Spot & Margin Trading** or **Enable Withdrawals**.
BINANCE_FUTURES.ip: Pick the unrestricted option if you self-host on a changing address. Binance grants nothing beyond reading on an unrestricted key, which is exactly the scope wanted here.
BINANCE_FUTURES.secret: The **Secret Key** is shown only once, immediately after creation. Copy it before leaving the page.
BINANCE_FUTURES.note: If futures reads fail with a permission error, the key predates your Futures account — delete it and create a new one.

steps: Profile → **Account & Security** → **API Management**, then **Create New Key**.
Choose **System-generated API Keys**.
For **API Key Usage** pick **API Transaction**, and name the key.
Copy the **API Key** and **API Secret** into the fields above.
BYBIT.permissions: Select **Read-Only**, then tick the boxes under **Unified Trading** (Positions, Orders, Trade). Never **Read-Write**, and never a withdrawal or transfer box.
BYBIT.ip: Bybit expires keys with no IP bound after 3 months. Bind your server's address if it is fixed; otherwise plan on replacing the key every 90 days with **Replace credentials**, which keeps the history already imported.
BYBIT.secret: The **API Secret** appears once, at creation, and never again.
BYBIT.note: A brand-new Bybit account has to wait 48 hours after registering before it can create API keys.

steps: Profile → **API** to open API management, then **Create API key**.
Name the key and link it to the account whose history you want.
Invent a **Passphrase** — see below.
Copy the **API key**, **Secret key** and passphrase into the fields above.
OKX.passphrase: OKX asks you to invent a passphrase while creating the key; it is not your account password. OKX keeps only a hash of it and can never show it again, so write it down and paste it into **API passphrase** above.
OKX.ip: Optional, up to 20 addresses. Only keys with **Trade** or **Withdraw** and no IP bound expire (after 14 idle days), so a read-only key is safe to leave unbound.
OKX.secret: The **Secret key** and the passphrase are both shown only at creation. Lose either one and the key has to be recreated.

steps: Profile icon → **API Management**, then **Create API key**.
Choose **System-generated API key**.
Add a note (the key's name) and set an **API passphrase** — see below.
Complete the email, SMS or 2FA verification Bitget asks for.
Copy the **API Key** and **Secret Key** into the fields above.
BITGET.permissions: Set every permission group to **Read-only** — on a Unified Trading Account that means **Trade → Read-only** (plus **Management → Read-only** if shown). Never read-write, never withdrawal.
BITGET.passphrase: You choose the API passphrase during creation, and Bitget can neither show nor reset it afterwards: a forgotten passphrase means recreating the key. Paste it into **API passphrase** above.
BITGET.ip: Bitget recommends binding an address. Leave it empty if your self-hosted IP is dynamic.
BITGET.secret: The **Secret Key** is displayed once, at creation. Copy it along with the passphrase you chose.
BITGET.note: Use this source only if your account is on the **Unified Trading Account**. If it is not, use **Bitget Classic** instead — Bitget itself rejects the wrong generation of key.

steps: Profile icon → **API Management**, then **Create API key**.
Choose **System-generated API key**.
Add a note (the key's name) and set an **API passphrase** — see below.
Complete the email, SMS or 2FA verification Bitget asks for.
Copy the **API Key** and **Secret Key** into the fields above.
BITGET_CLASSIC.permissions: Set every permission group to **Read-only**, **Futures** included — that is where your closed positions come from. Never read-write, never withdrawal.
BITGET_CLASSIC.passphrase: You choose the API passphrase during creation, and Bitget can neither show nor reset it afterwards: a forgotten passphrase means recreating the key. Paste it into **API passphrase** above.
BITGET_CLASSIC.ip: Bitget recommends binding an address. Leave it empty if your self-hosted IP is dynamic.
BITGET_CLASSIC.secret: The **Secret Key** is displayed once, at creation. Copy it along with the passphrase you chose.
BITGET_CLASSIC.note: Use this source only if your account has **not** been upgraded to a Unified Trading Account. If it has, use plain **Bitget** — a UTA key is rejected here.

steps: Sign in at futures.kraken.com — Kraken's futures platform is a separate account from Kraken spot, with its own keys.
Click your name (top right) → **Settings**, then the **Create Key** tab of the API panel.
Press **Create Key**, then copy the **Public key** into the API key field above and the **Private key** into the API secret field.
KRAKEN_FUTURES.permissions: Set the general API permission to **Read Only** — not **Full Access**. Leave the withdrawal permission at **No Access**.
KRAKEN_FUTURES.ip: Kraken Futures does not ask for an IP whitelist, so there is nothing to choose for a self-hosted setup.
KRAKEN_FUTURES.secret: Kraken says it plainly: the private key is displayed only once. Copy it before leaving the page.
KRAKEN_FUTURES.note: A Kraken Futures key does not work for Kraken Spot, or the other way round. Fees are not imported here — Kraken documents that the fee values its futures API returns no longer match what was charged.

steps: Sign in to Kraken Pro, open the menu (top right) → **Settings** → the **API** tab, then **Create API key**.
Give the key a unique **Key description**.
Leave **Nonce window** and the optional **Key expiry** at their defaults.
Generate the key, then copy the **API key** into the API key field above and the **Private key** into the API secret field.
KRAKEN_SPOT.permissions: Tick only **Query closed orders & trades** — that single query is all tradelog reads. Leave **Create & modify orders**, **Cancel/close orders**, **Deposit funds** and **Withdraw funds** off.
KRAKEN_SPOT.ip: Optional. Leave the IP restriction empty unless your server has a fixed address.
KRAKEN_SPOT.secret: The **Private key** is shown once, at creation. Store it like a password.
KRAKEN_SPOT.note: This is Kraken's spot platform — a different account and balance from Kraken Futures. Its first sync walks back years in small windows and paces itself against Kraken's rate limit, so expect it to take a while.

steps: Sign in to Gate, hover the profile icon and open **API Management** (also reachable as Personal Center → **Sub account and API** → **APIv4 Keys**).
Click **Create API Key** and pick **API v4 Key** as the type.
Enter an **API Key Remark** — the key's name — and select the account the history belongs to.
Confirm with your fund password and 2FA, then copy the **Key** and **Secret** into the fields above.
GATEIO_FUTURES.permissions: In the permission list set **Perpetual Futures** to **Read Only** and leave every other row off — **Withdraw** above all. Never **Read and Write**.
GATEIO_FUTURES.ip: Optional. Leave **Bind IP** blank if your self-hosted address is dynamic.
GATEIO_FUTURES.secret: The **Secret** is shown only at creation. Copy it before closing the dialog.

steps: Complete KYC verification first — MEXC only grants futures API permission to verified accounts.
Profile icon → **API Management** to open the API page, then create a new key.
Add a note (the key's name) and set the permissions below.
Pass the security verification, then copy the **Access Key** and **Secret Key** into the fields above.
MEXC_FUTURES.permissions: Enable only the read/query permission for **Futures**. No order placement, no transfers, no withdrawal.
MEXC_FUTURES.ip: MEXC expires keys with no IP bound after 90 days, renewable from 5 days before expiry. Bind your server's address if it is fixed; otherwise plan on replacing the key quarterly with **Replace credentials**.
MEXC_FUTURES.secret: MEXC shows the **Secret Key** only once and says so — store it immediately.
MEXC_FUTURES.note: MEXC restricts futures API access, so even a correctly configured new key can be refused outright. A permissions error on the first sync is that restriction rather than a mistake in your setup.

steps: Profile avatar → **API Management**, then **Create API**.
Choose **Link Third-Party Applications**: that type cannot withdraw and needs no IP address. (**API Trading** works too if you would rather bind one.)
Enter an **API Name** and an **API Passphrase** you invent — see below.
Confirm with your trading password, the email code and your 2FA code.
Copy the **API Key** and **API Secret** into the fields above.
KUCOIN_FUTURES.permissions: Tick **General** only — that is KuCoin's read-only scope. Leave **Spot Trading**, **Futures Trading**, **Margin Trading**, **Transfer** and **Withdrawal** unticked.
KUCOIN_FUTURES.passphrase: You invent the API passphrase while creating the key, and KuCoin never shows it again. Paste it into **API passphrase** above.
KUCOIN_FUTURES.ip: Not required for a third-party-app key. On an **API Trading** key, add your server's address if it is fixed.
KUCOIN_FUTURES.secret: Key, secret and passphrase cannot be recovered once lost — copy all three the moment they appear.
KUCOIN_FUTURES.note: One KuCoin key covers the futures API host as well; tradelog reads only your closed futures positions.

steps: Open Quantfury and go to **Trading History** — in the side menu of the mobile app, or the main menu of the web platform.
Open the **Closed Positions** tab.
Optionally tap the filter icon (top right) to narrow the report; importing is idempotent, so the filter you pick does not matter.
At the bottom of the page, tap the **PDF** icon to download the **Trading History Report**.
Back here, choose that PDF in the upload card, press **Preview** to check what was found, then **Import**.
QUANTFURY.note: Quantfury has no API, so nothing syncs on its own — export again whenever you want to catch up, and re-importing skips duplicates. Download the **PDF** report: Quantfury's Excel export is a different layout that tradelog does not parse.

journalCsv.hint: Upload a CSV of closed positions in tradelog's canonical format (below). Ideal for hand-kept journals or dead exchanges. Re-uploading the same file is safe (duplicates are updated in place).
journalCsv.warnClosedBeforeOpened: {{count}} row(s) have a close date earlier than the open date — check those entries.
journalCsv.warnOverlap: {{count}} row(s) look like positions already imported from another source in this profile. Importing them would double-count their PnL.

format.ai_hint: Tip: paste this whole reference into any AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, …) together with your old trade history — a screenshot, a PDF statement, or a messy spreadsheet from an exchange that no longer exists — and ask it to produce a CSV that follows exactly this format. Then come back here, Preview to validate, and Import.
format.intro: Dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) or dot (.) decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting (wrap a field in double quotes if it contains ;, " or a line break). First row is the literal header below; one closed position per row. Lines starting with # are ignored.
format.pnlNote: realized_pnl is the result BEFORE fees (gross). Leave it empty to have it computed as (exit_price − entry_price) × quantity, negated for shorts. Put commissions in fees.
format.notionalNote: No per-unit price? Set quantity to 1 and use the TOTAL position value as entry_price (amount invested / notional) and exit_price (amount returned) — not your margin.

cols.symbol: Base asset or BASE/QUOTE, e.g. BTC or SUI/USDT. Quote defaults to USDT.
cols.opened_at: Open date: YYYY-MM-DD, or an instant YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (UTC).
cols.closed_at: Close date, same format as opened_at.
cols.quantity: Base-asset units. Use 1 if you only have totals. Defaults to 1.
cols.entry_price: Per-unit entry price — or total invested when quantity=1.
cols.exit_price: Per-unit exit price — or total returned when quantity=1.
cols.realized_pnl: Gross result before fees. Empty = computed from prices.
cols.exchange: Venue this trade came from (e.g. FTX). Becomes the position's exchange; if blank, this data source's label is used. Spelling doesn't matter: a venue tradelog connects to (Bitunix, BingX, BitMart, Quantfury) is stored under its usual name, so the rows merge with what syncs.

quantfury.title: Quantfury PDF import
quantfury.hint: Upload the Quantfury "Trading History Report" PDF. Closed positions are parsed and imported; re-uploading is safe (duplicates are skipped).

taxonomy.title: Tags (Origen)
taxonomy.hint: Customize the tags you can assign to positions. Each group is single-select per position.
taxonomy.archivedHint: Archived tags can't be assigned to new positions, but the positions that already carry them keep them.

settings.timeZoneHint: Your active time zone. It sets the day boundaries everywhere: analytics buckets, capital snapshots, adjustments and ROI periods.

capital.title: Trading capital & risk
capital.historyHint: Capital is tracked as a dated history of adjustments and snapshots on the Capital page; the dashboard's risk figures use the estimated current capital derived from it.
capital.riskHint: The two percentages of capital you're willing to risk on a single trade. Used to show the maximum to lose per trade on the dashboard.
capital.frequencyHint: How often the background job records the estimated capital as a snapshot. Manually entered values always win — the job never overwrites them.
capital.backfillHint: Materializes the snapshot series at the frequency above, from your first adjustment through today, and refreshes stale values — without waiting for the background job. Manual values are never touched.
capital.backfillNeedsAnchor: Create your first adjustment on the Capital page to enable backfilling.
capital.timeZoneNote: Active time zone: {{tz}}. It sets the day boundaries for snapshots, adjustments and ROI periods — change it in Account above.

capital.title: Capital
capital.timeZoneNote: Time zone: {{tz}} — day boundaries for snapshots, adjustments and ROI periods use it.

estimated.title: Current estimated capital
estimated.hint: Your latest adjustment per exchange, carried forward with the net PnL of trades closed since.
estimated.empty: No adjustments yet. Your capital history starts with the first adjustment — add it below.

adjustments.title: Adjustment history
adjustments.hint: An adjustment records your real balance per exchange on a date (at the start of that day, in your time zone). It is the truth at that point and a hard cut: earlier trades stop counting — estimates and ROI continue from it.
adjustments.firstMandatory: The first adjustment is the starting point of your capital history. ROI and the capital chart stay empty until you add it.
adjustments.addHint: Fill in the balance of the exchanges you want to anchor on that date; leave the rest empty.
adjustments.deleteConfirm: Delete this adjustment? Later days will be re-estimated from the previous one.

snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.hint: Estimated capital at the start of each day, recorded by the background job at your configured frequency. Editing a value turns that day into an adjustment (anchor) for that exchange — the job never overwrites manual values. Clear a manual value to return the day to automatic. Empty or 0 means no capital that day.
snapshots.manualTitle: Manual value (anchor) — the job never overwrites it
snapshots.deleteDayConfirm: Delete this day's stored snapshot? Manual values on it are adjustments and will be removed too — later days are re-estimated from the previous adjustment. Days matching your snapshot frequency are re-created automatically; deleting is permanent only for days outside the current frequency.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.description: Download a portable JSON copy of everything in your account — profiles, tags, and your full position history with fills and annotations. API keys are not included.
backup.restoreHint: Restoring replaces ALL of your current data with the file's contents. Use it to rebuild from scratch; you'll re-enter API keys afterwards.
backup.replaceWarning: This replaces ALL your current profiles, data sources and positions with the contents of this file. API keys are not in the backup — you'll re-enter them afterwards to resume syncing. This cannot be undone.
backup.imported: Restored {{profiles}} profile(s) and {{positions}} position(s). Re-enter your API keys to resume syncing.
backup.invalidFile: That file isn't a valid tradelog backup.

analytics.title: Dashboard
analytics.noData: No closed positions yet. Add a data source or import a trade history.

capital.title: Trading capital & risk
capital.info: Your estimated current capital — the latest adjustment per exchange carried forward with the net PnL of trades closed since — and the maximum to lose per trade. It uses the Exchange filter only and does not change with the Period or Origen filters.
capital.emptyCta: Create your first adjustment on the Capital page
capital.capitalInfo: Sum of your estimated current capital across the selected exchange(s).
capital.maxLossInfo: Capital × risk %. The maximum to lose on a single trade — not the position size.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.info: Key figures over the filtered set of closed trades. PnL is net of fees and funding.
stats.totalPnlInfo: Sum of the net result of every trade in the set.
stats.roiInfo: Net PnL of the period's trades — counted from your most recent capital adjustment (the hard cut) — divided by your capital at the first day of the period (that day's snapshot or adjustment). Blank when no snapshot or adjustment exists at or before the period start. Follows the Period and Exchange filters but NOT Origen: capital isn't tagged by origen.
stats.volumeInfo: Total notional traded across the set, counting both legs: quantity × (entry price + exit price), summed over every trade.
stats.winRateInfo: Share of trades with a positive result. Break-even trades (0) are excluded.
stats.avgWinInfo: Mean net result of winning trades.
stats.avgLossInfo: Mean net result of losing trades.
stats.expectancyInfo: Expected result per trade: (win rate × average win) − (loss rate × |average loss|).
stats.avgRRInfo: Average win divided by the absolute average loss.

analytics.cumulativeProfitInfo: Running sum of net results ordered by close date — your equity curve.
analytics.capitalEvolutionInfo: Your stored capital snapshots, stacked per exchange. This is capital over time and INCLUDES your manual adjustments (deposits, withdrawals, corrections) — it is not trading return; for that, see Cumulative profit. The markers flag days with a manual adjustment. Benchmarks are off by default: each one projects the capital held at the start of the visible range forward at that asset's price, anchored per exchange on its own first day so adding an exchange mid-range is not read as growth. It is a lump sum in USD — capital added later is not projected, and it is not what you would have made trading.
analytics.capitalEvolutionSubtitle: Capital over time, including your adjustments — not trading return.
analytics.capitalEvolutionEmpty: No capital snapshots yet. Create your first adjustment on the Capital page.
analytics.activityInfo: Count of long and short trades per day, with each day's win rate.
analytics.pnlPerDayInfo: Total net result for each day of the month.
analytics.monthlySummaryInfo: Net result per month with the monthly win rate.
analytics.monthlyRoiInfo: ROI for each month of the year: net PnL of trades closed that month (from the most recent adjustment before/within the month) divided by capital at the first day of that month. Gaps indicate no capital data at or before the start of that month, not 0% ROI. Cumulative ROI and 3-month avg are computed strictly from existing monthly data, never projected; 3-month avg requires 3 consecutive months of real data to show a point. Benchmarks are off by default — click one to compare. They show that asset's buy-and-hold return for the same month (price at month end ÷ price at month start − 1), always in USD, for comparison only: they are not part of your ROI. A benchmark month without price data is a gap, not 0%.
analytics.winRateByHourInfo: Win rate and number of trades for each hour of the day, in your time zone.
analytics.winRateByWeekdayInfo: Win rate and number of trades for each weekday, in your time zone.
analytics.directionInfo: Long vs short: number of trades, win rate, total PnL and expectancy.
analytics.traderStyleInfo: Trades grouped by holding time: scalper (< 15m), day trader (15m–24h), swing (> 24h).
analytics.winningStreaksInfo: Average winning-streak length and the net PnL of the longest winning streak.
analytics.losingStreaksInfo: Average losing-streak length and the net PnL of the longest losing streak.
analytics.recoveryInfo: How often the trade after a loss is a win.
analytics.calendarInfo: Total net PnL for each day of the month, colored by sign.
analytics.mostTradedInfo: Pairs ranked by number of trades.
analytics.mostProfitableInfo: Pairs ranked by positive total PnL.
analytics.leastProfitableInfo: Pairs ranked by negative total PnL.
analytics.feesInfo: Total fees for each day of the month.
analytics.cumulativeFeesInfo: Running sum of fees over time.
analytics.feeRatioInfo: Per-day return on fees: net PnL ÷ fees. Month value is month PnL ÷ month fees, from monthly totals. Days with no trades or zero fees are skipped.
analytics.benchmarkNoData: No price data yet — the background job has not filled this series.
analytics.benchmarkNoDataForYear: No data for this year — this series does not cover it.
analytics.benchmarkNoDataForRange: This series does not reach back to the start of the visible range.
analytics.capitalBenchmarkNote: Lump-sum comparison: the capital already held at the start of the visible range, projected forward at the benchmark's price. Capital added after that point is NOT included, so deposits make the two diverge.

sync.skipped: Sync already in progress — try again shortly

quickSync.label: Quick sync
quickSync.noExchanges: No exchange sources to sync. Add Bitunix or BingX in Settings.
